data.title: Bihar govt introduces performance assessment index for banks
data.description:
The Bihar government has for the first time introduced a 100-point performance assessment index to rank banks operating in the state, a senior official said on Saturday.

IDFC FIRST Bank currently tops the list with 74 points, Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh said.

“Banks have been classified into three zones based on their score. The Green Zone, indicating excellent performance, includes 11 banks scoring 50 or above, while seven banks fall in the Yellow Zone and several others in the Red Zone. The Red Zone includes leading public sector banks,” a statement issued by the state’s Finance Department said.

Bihar has set an annual credit plan target of ₹4.95 lakh crore for the 2026-27 fiscal. As of September 30, banks disbursed ₹1.89 lakh crore, achieving 38.25 per cent of the target, officials said.

The figure was ₹46,228.29 crore higher than that of the corresponding period last year.

“The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector recorded 52.68 per cent achievement, with credit disbursement of ₹84,091.21 crore against a target of ₹1.59 lakh crore. Agriculture credit disbursement stood at ₹43,967.17 crore, or 28 per cent of the target,” the release said.

At a high-level review meeting here, Singh directed banks to work in mission mode to achieve their annual credit plan targets, stressing that deposits mobilised in Bihar must be reinvested in the state's development.

Senior officials of the Finance Department, the State Level Bankers' Committee, public and private sector banks, were among those who were part of the meeting.

data.title: KEC International bags orders worth ₹2,872 cr from Power Grid Corporation of India

data.title: Piyush Goyal concludes two-day Germany visit, holds high-level talks to boost trade, investment and technology ties
data.description:
Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal concluded his two-day official visit to Germany, holding a series of high-level meetings in Berlin aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, research and emerging technologies, as per a statement by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

According to an official statement, Goyal's engagements on October 23 included discussions with senior German government officials, business leaders, research institutions and members of the Indian diaspora, highlighting opportunities to deepen economic and industrial ties between the two countries.

During the visit, Goyal held a bilateral meeting with Levin Holle, Economic and Financial Policy Advisor and G7/G20 Sherpa at the German Federal Chancellery. “The discussions covered bilateral economic cooperation and opportunities to further strengthen economic and investment ties between India and Germany,” the Ministry said.

Goyal also held separate meetings with Siemens Healthineers AG CEO Bernd Montag, Bertelsmann Executive Board Member and Bertelsmann Investments CEO Carsten Coesfeld, and Volkswagen AG CFO and Škoda Auto CEO Holger Peters to explore opportunities for expanding business partnerships, investments and industrial cooperation between India and Germany.

He also participated in a roundtable with leading German industrial research institutions to discuss collaboration in advanced industrial technologies and innovation. “Separately, members of the accompanying Indian business delegation participated in sectoral roundtables with German industry representatives and sectoral associations to explore opportunities for bilateral business collaboration,” the release added.

Apart from this, he also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Berlin and addressed the media. Goyal also interacted with Indian science and technology researchers and students based in Germany and held a roundtable with heads of select Fraunhofer Institutes to explore collaboration in microelectronics, power electronics, logistics, smart manufacturing, industrial innovation and battery technologies.

The discussions focused on strengthening research cooperation and industry-academia partnerships between India and Germany. As per government data, India's bilateral trade with Germany stood at $31.03 billion in FY2025-26, with Indian exports to the country registering an 8.44 per cent year-on-year growth compared to FY2024-25, reflecting stronger export performance and sustained bilateral trade ties.

data.title: India's emerging sectors to drive capex, credit demand towards storage, semiconductors: Report
data.description:
Financing demand in India’s emerging sectors is expected to shift towards battery storage, semiconductor packaging, green hydrogen projects with assured buyers and defence suppliers over the next three to five years, as investments in new growth industries create opportunities for banks, according to a Union Bank of India research report.

The report noted artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and defence is likely to lead the investment pipeline, with indicative public and private investments of around ₹5.9 lakh crore, ₹5.27 lakh crore and ₹5.07 lakh crore, respectively. It said financing opportunities would increasingly emerge in advanced packaging and assembly of semiconductors, battery recycling, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion battery capacity, storage infrastructure and component suppliers to the defence industry.

The report also highlighted the potential for financing hydrogen projects backed by assured offtake agreements, while demand for data centres is expected to expand towards edge and colocation facilities as AI inference grows. However, the report cautioned that technology obsolescence, uncertain revenues, delayed payments and long investment payback periods remain significant risks for lenders.

Semiconductor projects typically have payback periods of five to eight years, while space projects may take seven to ten years, exceeding conventional loan tenures, it said. AI infrastructure also faces rapid technology cycles, with graphics processing unit clusters requiring upgrades every 18 to 24 months. The report said ten of the twelve emerging sectors already had identifiable debt-financing routes, while AI and space remained predominantly equity-funded due to technology risks and long payback periods. It recommended that banks develop specialised lending capabilities for semiconductors, hydrogen, data centres and battery storage, alongside products such as milestone-linked disbursements, receivables financing, equipment leasing and green loans.

The report identified renewable energy, semiconductors, green hydrogen and critical minerals as sectors suited to project finance and development finance institution-led funding, while electric vehicles and drones could benefit from asset financing and non-banking financial company lending.

India’s renewable energy capacity stood at 288.6 GW against a target of 500 GW by 2030, while the electric vehicle and battery storage market was projected to grow from $34 billion to $113 billion by 2030. The report said financing opportunities would increasingly move towards commercially viable projects and supply-chain participants as these emerging sectors expand.

data.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22% as EBITDA slips on fuel price freeze
data.description:
State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs.

BPCL's standalone net profit declined to ₹4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from ₹6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement.

Revenue from operations rose to ₹1.58 lakh crore from ₹1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to ₹9,437 crore from ₹10,968 crore.

India's second largest fuel retailer earned $32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to $10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back.

But these gains were wiped away by losses arising from the five month old freeze in retail price revision despite a rise in cost.

BPCL also booked ₹330 crore marketing inventory loss and another ₹397 crore loss due to forex fluctuation.

On a consolidated basis, net profit dropped 21.5 per cent to ₹4,863 crore from ₹6,191 crore, while revenue climbed 29.8 per cent to ₹1.58 lakh crore. Consolidated EBITDA declined 13.4 per cent to ₹9,647 crore.

The divergence between revenue growth and lower earnings highlights the pressure on profitability, even as the firm stepped up investments in refining, gas distribution and alternative fuels.

BPCL reported refinery throughput of 10.41 million tonne in the quarter, operating at 118 per cent of capacity, while domestic market sales stood at 13.47 million tonne. Its refineries had processed 9.82 million tonne of crude oil and sold 12.67 million tonne of fuel in the second quarter of the last fiscal.

The company said it continued investing in infrastructure, supply-chain resilience and digital transformation, while ensuring uninterrupted fuel supplies across the country.

BPCL also has advanced plans for a proposed 10-million-tonne-per-year (MMTPA) greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh. Its board approved the incorporation of a wholly-owned subsidiary to serve as the dedicated project company, subject to the requisite government, statutory and regulatory approvals.

The proposed complex would expand BPCL's refining and petrochemical footprint, although the announcement did not specify the project's investment outlay or construction timeline.

BPCL also commissioned the Matia LPG bottling plant in Goalpara, Assam, its first such facility in the Northeast, as it seeks to strengthen regional supply infrastructure. The company connected 1.22 lakh new households to Piped Natural Gas (PNG) over the past six months.

On the consumer front, BPCL launched Bharatgas Lite ZIP, a premium LPG offering aimed at improving service convenience, and rolled out more than 9,000 clean, hygienic and odour-free Drive Fresh washrooms across its retail network.

The company continued its 'Zero Ka Dum' programme to improve LPG quality and consumer safety, while expanding its 'Defect Mila Toh Refill Free' initiative, which is now operational in 14 cities.

BPCL said it also stepped up efforts to develop specialised fuels and lower-carbon alternatives. It developed Extreme Weather Grade (XWG) diesel for the Indian Army, designed for military vehicles operating in severe winter conditions and at high altitudes.

In aviation, the company operated a commercial flight using aviation turbine fuel blended with 1 per cent sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), marking a step in its efforts to explore lower-carbon fuel options. The announcement did not disclose the flight's route, the volume of blended fuel used or plans for wider commercial deployment.

Separately, BPCL partnered with Tiki Tar and Shell India Private Limited (TTSIPL) to expand its value-added bitumen portfolio.

BPCL, India's second-largest oil marketing company, operates refineries in Mumbai, Kochi and Bina with combined capacity of about 35.3 million tonne per annum. Its retail network includes more than 25,300 fuel stations and over 6,250 LPG distributorships.

The company has set a target of becoming a net-zero energy company by 2040 for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, which cover direct emissions and those associated with purchased energy, respectively. Its investments in refining, natural gas infrastructure and alternative fuels form part of its broader effort to adapt its business to India's changing energy requirements.

data.title: Adani Wind bags 696 MW orders from five power producers, third-party book crosses 1 GW
data.description:
Adani Wind, the wind energy business of Adani New Industries Ltd, has secured orders totalling 696.2 megawatts (MW) from five power producers, expanding its customer base beyond the Adani Group as India's wind industry shifts towards higher-capacity turbines.

The orders comprise 300 MW from Purvah Green Power, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group; 155 MW from Jindal India Power, part of the BC Jindal Group; 109.2 MW from NTPC Renewable Energy; 82.5 MW from Aditya Birla Renewables; and 49.5 MW from Integrum Energy, according to people familiar with the matter.

The contracts cover three wind turbine generator platforms rated at 5.2 MW, 5 MW and 3.3 MW, with projects spread across Karnataka, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

With the latest orders, Adani Wind's cumulative order book from independent power producers outside its group has crossed 1 gigawatt (GW), marking a milestone in its efforts to build a third-party business in a market where turbine manufacturers are competing to supply equipment for India's expanding renewable energy capacity, they said.

The largest order, from Purvah Green Power, covers 60 wind turbines rated at 5 MW each for deployment in Bellary, Karnataka. Jindal India Power's 155 MW order comprises 31 turbines of the same rating for installation in Davanagere, Karnataka.

NTPC Renewable Energy has ordered 21 turbines rated at 5.2 MW each for its Khavda project in Gujarat. The Aditya Birla Renewables and Integrum Energy orders will use Adani Wind's 3.3 MW turbine platform for projects in Bhuj, Gujarat and Nandurbar, Maharashtra, respectively, the people said.

The order wins come as Adani Wind seeks to scale up its manufacturing capacity at Mundra, Gujarat, from 2.25 GW annually to 5 GW, with a longer-term target of 10 GW. The expansion would position the company to compete for a larger share of domestic turbine demand and potentially serve overseas markets.

Adani Wind's 5 MW MWL-185 platform has an 185-metre rotor diameter and a 140-metre hub height and is designed for low- to moderate-wind conditions.

Its 5.2 MW MWL-160 platform is among the higher-capacity onshore turbine models listed under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM).

The company's MWL-160 platform has crossed 2 GW of installations at Khavda, which hosts a large renewable energy development in Gujarat, according to the people. All four of Adani Wind's turbine models are listed under the ministry's approved list, and the company is the only Indian wind turbine manufacturer included in BloombergNEF's global top 15 ranking for 2025.

India, the world's fourth-largest wind power market, has 59.2 GW of installed wind capacity, with a further 43 GW under implementation. The combined base of operational and under-development capacity exceeds 100 GW.

Domestic wind turbine manufacturing capacity has more than doubled from about 12 GW in fiscal 2023 to over 24 GW annually. The industry is targeting installations of around 8 GW in fiscal 2027, with annual additions projected to reach 13.2 GW by fiscal 2031.

India installed a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in fiscal 2026.

The sector is also moving towards larger turbines and rotor diameters, which can capture more wind energy and improve project economics, depending on local wind conditions, site constraints and infrastructure requirements. Higher-capacity machines can also help developers optimise land use in established wind corridors.

Adani Wind has a portfolio of turbine platforms ranging from 3 MW to 5 MW-plus and is exploring international markets. It has exported blade sets equipped with anti-icing technology to Europe and is engaging with potential customers in the United States, Australia, Brazil and Southeast Asia.

The latest contracts give Adani Wind an opportunity to broaden its customer base as it scales up manufacturing. Securing orders from independent power producers and established energy companies could help demonstrate the commercial acceptance of its technology, although the ultimate contribution to revenue will depend on delivery schedules, project execution and commissioning, analysts said.

data.title: PM Modi to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on October 25
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday (October 25), where he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, witness the Indian Air Force's aerial display at Namo Ghat and inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, according to a press release.

At around 11 am, the Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited's new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, followed by the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat at around 1 pm, where he will attend as the chief guest.

The garment manufacturing facility is expected to strengthen India's textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promote industrial growth in the region, the release stated.

Focusing on modern manufacturing practices, the facility will create employment opportunities, particularly for women, and contribute to the region's economic progress. With a global customer base, it will also enable products manufactured in Varanasi to reach international markets, the release added. The inauguration is expected to highlight Uttar Pradesh's growing role as a destination for industrial investment and manufacturing-led growth, while the predominantly women-led initiative reflects the focus on women-led development.

The Prime Minister will thereafter witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat, organised to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force under the theme "Wings over Ganges".

The aerial display will feature aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness in operations.

The Indian Air Force's premier display teams, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will participate in the event, demonstrating precision flying, coordination and operational excellence, according to the release. Thereafter, Modi will travel to Odisha, where he will inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar at around 4.45 pm and address the gathering.

The newly established facilities are aimed at strengthening the technological foundations of India's financial system by providing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the broader financial sector, the release stated. Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives.

The facility has been certified to the Uptime Institute Tier IV standard, a global benchmark for data centre infrastructure, placing it in the highest tier of operational resilience.

According to the release, the facility is among the largest Tier IV-certified facilities in the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector worldwide. It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services and provide a secure digital foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy.

It will also strengthen the RBI's position in digital infrastructure among central banks. The Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide a dedicated platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and capability development across the sector.

The institute will focus on cutting-edge technologies relevant to the BFSI sector, including quantum computing, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, the release added.

data.title: Patanjali Foods Faces Cow Ghee Recall Order In Madhya Pradesh
data.description:
The company said the order would have no material financial or operational impact beyond the value of the affected batch and confirmed plans to challenge the decision

Patanjali Foods has received an order to recall a batch of cow ghee after the product was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the company said in a stock exchange filing on Saturday, 24 October. The order was issued by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Madhya Pradesh.

The order, issued by the designated officer of the FDA in Burhanpur, relates to a sample of cow ghee that failed to meet the requirements prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, along with provisions governing contaminants, toxins and residues.

The FMCG company said the recall would not have any material impact on its financial or operational activities, apart from the value of the affected batch of cow ghee. It also informed the exchanges that it is filing an appeal against the order. In its regulatory filing, Patanjali Foods stated that it had received a “recall order of sale of Cow Ghee of a Batch on account of unsafe as per The Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.”

The development comes amid increased regulatory scrutiny of food safety and product labelling in India.

Recently, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issued a prohibition order directing Dabur India to stop selling food products carrying “100%” claims, stating that such labelling violates the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018. The prohibition covered several products, including honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, along with other food items carrying similar claims.

Separately, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has stepped up its statewide enforcement drive against food adulteration. The action has resulted in the seizure of suspected adulterated dairy products and sweets, including butter, khoya, paneer, ghee and shrikhand.

data.title: 'Non-answers' aren't working. This is what investors really need from the Fed.
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Chair Kevin Warsh has to make a U-turn in communication

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks during his news conference in September.

The headline coming out of the Federal Reserve's meeting Wednesday will be the central bank's decision on interest rates, but what really matters to investors, economists say, is for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to prove he can successfully communicate the central bank's strategy.

Analysts want to know whether the hot inflation readings for September were a game-changing development, and what criteria the Fed will use to assess the timing and pace of subsequent rate hikes. They'll be watching Warsh's press conference Wednesday for signs that the central bank has a strategy for curbing prices after more than five years of inflation above its 2% target.

"The market cares about the final destination," more than the outcome of Wednesday's meeting, said Juhi Dhawan, global macroanalyst at Wellington Management.

Right now, the market expects a "shallow" Fed tightening of up to three rate hikes by the end of the first quarter of 2027. There have been many periods when the Fed has tightened only a few times, she said. That strategy fits with the narrative that the Fed is reversing the three cuts the central bank made last year over concern about the labor market.

There's a possibility they could take a more aggressive approach with a full rate hike. A "full" rate-hiking cycle would be 150 or 200 basis points, Dhawan said, which would take rates back up to the highest levels since 2023.

Derek Tang, co-founder of forecasting firm LH Meyer, said the market has a very difficult time understanding when the rate hikes will end.

"Do the hikes end when inflation literally is at 2%?" Tang asked.

Previous Fed chairs have provided a forecast, such as saying something like: The Fed can hike until underlying inflation gets low enough and then the central bank will hold rates steady. But Warsh hasn't provided any signals about the Fed's approach.

"It is a little bit of a black box," Tang said. "He's become quite skilled at giving non-answers."

The ultimate level of rates will impact borrowers and homebuyers. If rates go high enough, it could even choke off the current economic expansion.

A less-is-more approach

When Warsh came into office in May, he installed a sea change in Fed communication that can best be summed up as "less is more." A quieter Fed would let the market speak louder, he said.

This approach has proven to be a mistake, said Nicholas Economides, a professor of economics at the Stern School of Business at New York University.

"The new Fed chair has missed his chance to define policy coherently by proposing to 'listen to the market,' when the market in fact wants to listen to him," Economides said in an interview.

Warsh's silence on his views on the path forward for interest rates essentially gives away the Fed's authority to the market, he added.

"Unless the Fed speaks authoritatively, over and above what market considerations are, it will just lose its voice," Economides said.

He pointed to market moves after the Fed's September rate hike as an example.

At his September press conference, Warsh declined to answer whether he thought the first hike in three years would be a one-off event or the start of a series of hikes.

Without any guidance, markets pushed interest rates on longer-term Treasurys significantly higher, with the 10-year yield rising to 5.3%, as the market priced in an aggressive Fed with a rate hike in October.

-Greg Robb

data.title: China's Communist Party names new provincial chiefs ahead of fifth plenum
data.description:
By Eduardo Baptista

China's ruling Communist Party announced key personnel changes in six provinces on Saturday, two days before it holds a closed-door conclave in Beijing from October 26 to 29.

The official focus of the secretive meeting, also known as a plenum, in the Chinese capital is expected to be party governance and discipline, though personnel issues could also feature.

Here are the appointments:

  • State Council Vice Secretary-General Wang Zhijun was named Communist Party secretary of the southern province of Hunan, replacing Shen Xiaoming

  • Wang is a full member of the Central Committee, the ​largest of the party's top decision-making bodies

  • Mo Gaoyi, a vice minister at the party's publicity department and director of the State Council Information Office, was named party secretary of the southwestern province of Yunnan, replacing Wang Ning

  • Xie Weijiang, Hunan's deputy party secretary and party chief of Yueyang, a city in the province's northeast, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Mao Weiming

  • Guo Ningning, Fujian's deputy party secretary and party chief of the provincial capital Fuzhou, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling she is set to become governor

Tezos is a distinctive blockchain platform architected to facilitate and govern decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts. Its foundation is built on a decentralized governance system that enables blockchain modifications through a community-led decision-making process.

Emma Tucker

1. FROM MY DESK

The world's richest people are embracing a new form of philanthropy: giving a couple hundred dollars to children, one investment account at a time.

Elon Musk is pledging (SpaceX) shares to millions of kids, joining Michael Dell and other billionaires in seeding the new Trump Accounts program. The effort comes as Silicon Valley titans are increasingly cast as societal villains. Communities across the country are opposing data centers, and some polling shows many Americans say they want billionaires to have less political, economic and cultural power.

The payouts idea came from tech investor Brad Gerstner, who sold the concept to the White House and envisions it as a new social contract between the wealthiest Americans and the rest of society. Critics see a political stunt packed with tax advantages for the ultrarich. Erich Schwartzel and Konrad Putzier explore whether these giveaways can keep the pitchforks at bay.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • House Democrats are targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, weighing impeachment as one of their first moves if they take back the House in the midterms.
  • A wave of AI-powered attacks has hit the internet in recent weeks, as hackers armed with agents and other tools make intrusions faster and far harder to trace.
  • The yellow-vest protest movement paralyzed Paris eight years ago. Now it is re-emerging as part of a coalition across France demanding solutions to the high cost of living and other economic complaints.
  • Ukraine said its Starlink system was working normally again, raising hopes of an end to the dayslong disruption to the vital satellite internet service by Elon Musk's SpaceX was ending.
  • An Anduril-backed startup is genetically engineering military dogs to run faster, have a keener sense of smell and avoid inherited diseases.
  • Our national security correspondent got rare access to a U.S. aircraft carrier conducting missions in the Strait of Hormuz, as it prepares for potential strikes on Iranian targets.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • To the scientific world, Moderna's cancer vaccine's results proved that a highly personalized, immune-targeting medication can work. To investors, it didn't work well enough, with shares tanking. Columnist David Wainer writes that even after the sharp fall, the drugmaker's stock assumes wild successes.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

Government grift emerges as a defining midterm issue.

Less than two weeks before the midterms, corruption is suddenly eclipsing inflation as voters' top concern. A string of damaging headlines about the president's inner circle-ranging from a longtime adviser facing a Justice Department inquiry, to a Russian businessman funding his son's lavish wedding afterparty-has left Republican operatives wringing their hands. With Democrats hammering the issue in ads, strategists worry these self-dealing allegations could make a challenging election even harder. Our reporters break down the growing anxiety, and why the fallout could cost Republicans at the ballot box.

5.

The secret playbook behind A24's Elizabeth Holmes smash hit.

For nearly three years, indie studio A24 pulled off a minor Hollywood miracle: keeping its Elizabeth Holmes documentary a complete secret-even from most of its employees. Fewer than 10 staffers knew directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had embedded with the convicted Theranos fraudster just weeks before she reported to federal prison. That secrecy eventually became the film's most potent marketing weapon. "You Can See Everything" scored a $15 million box-office debut-the biggest for a non-music documentary since 2004. John Jurgensen and Ben Fritz reveal how the studio turned a stealth production into a massive cultural phenomenon.

6. SEE THE STORY

You were once smarter than AI at math. Yes, even you.

Five years ago, frontier AI models could barely pass a basic arithmetic test. Today, those same systems have graduated from grade-school homework to solving open research problems that eluded humans for decades. Columnist Ben Cohen looks at how AI went from failing simple math to transforming the field forever. Can you beat the early AI models? Take the quiz.

57

That is the median age for becoming a grandmother today, up from 44 in 1960. Because Americans are waiting longer to have children, this demographic shift is shrinking the healthy years grandparents get to spend actively involved with their grandkids from 28 years down to just 15. But there is a silver lining: Older, retired people are more likely to have time to be with grandchildren, and spending on each grandchild grows as family sizes shrink.

9. AND FINALLY...

The biggest No. 1 in Billboard history is one you might not have heard.

Ella Langley's country hit "Choosin' Texas" recently broke a Billboard Hot 100 record by spending 24 weeks in the top spot, dethroning Mariah Carey. With attention split across a million platforms and highly personalized TikTok algorithms, old mainstream unifiers like radio and TV have lost much of their power. And because the hit didn't top the streaming charts in markets like New York and Los Angeles, it shows how a massive multiweek No. 1 can easily pass people by when media is no longer centralized.

data.title: Wingify Appoints Sahil Sharma As Global Chief People Officer

Sharma joins Wingify after a decade at RateGain, where he held senior HR roles spanning people strategy, organisational development and talent management

Wingify has appointed Sahil Sharma as its global chief people officer, effective October 2026. He joins the software company after a decade at RateGain, where he held several senior human resources leadership positions, most recently serving as group chief human resources officer and chair of RGForALL.

Sharma brings experience across people strategy, organisational development, performance management, talent acquisition, employer branding and learning. His career spans technology, business-to-business software-as-a-service (SaaS), digital media and healthcare services.

Leadership Role At RateGain

Sharma served as group chief human resources officer and chair of RGForALL at RateGain from October 2022 to October 2026. He joined the company in 2016 as senior manager for global learning and organisational effectiveness before taking on broader responsibilities, including the role of associate vice-president of human resources.

During his tenure, he worked across people and culture leadership, HR transformation, cross-border mergers and acquisitions, and initial public offering (IPO) journeys.

Earlier Career In HR

Before joining RateGain, Sharma spent four years at IndiaMART InterMESH in strategic HR and learning roles. From July 2012 to May 2015, he served as manager of learning and capacity development, overseeing learning initiatives across India. He later became senior manager of strategic human resources within the HR Centre of Excellence.

Sharma began his career at Serco in 2009, working in training roles supporting a US healthcare client. He served as a process trainer before becoming team leader for training.

Focus On People Strategy

Beyond human resources, Sharma has led sales enablement and customer experience initiatives, bringing a business-oriented perspective to people strategy. He has also advocated the use of artificial intelligence to improve HR processes and business performance.

At Wingify, he will lead the company's global people function, drawing on his experience in talent development, organisational effectiveness and aligning HR priorities with business objectives.

Academic And Advisory Roles

Sharma holds qualifications in business administration and management from Cornell University and in human resource management from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta.

He is also a member of the Board of Advisors at Chandigarh University, a position he took up in June 2026.

Finance Experience Across Functions

Jain is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). His experience spans commercial finance, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), and manufacturing finance, including roles in India and international markets.

Wider Leadership Changes

The finance transition coincides with the conclusion of Pralhad Bhutada’s employment agreement as managing director and chief executive officer of Elica India on 31 March 2027. His role and board membership will end on that date.

Ahuja, who became chief operating officer on 1 September 2026, will succeed Bhutada as managing director from 1 April 2027 and report to Elica India’s board chairman.

data.title: NANOBIOTIX Announces Final Data from Phase 1 Study Evaluating JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors as a 2L+ Therapy in Anti-PD-1-Resistant Primary Cutaneous Melanoma
data.description:
Key points:
  • In 24 heavily pre-treated patients with advanced primary cutaneous melanoma whose cancer had progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy including anti-PD-1 therapy, data continue to show an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy
  • 41.7% (10/24) overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1, including 4 complete responses
  • 75% (18/24) disease control rate (DCR)
  • 17.8 months median Overall Survival
  • Exploratory analysis in a subset of patients (n=8) identified IL-1β, a cytokine linked to treatment-induced anti-tumor immunity, as the most increased plasma cytokine after treatment
  • Investigators concluded that these preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in randomized clinical trials for patients with primary cutaneous melanoma naïve or refractory to anti-PD-1

Data presented at the 2026 Congress of the European Society for Medical Oncology

PARIS and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NANOBIOTIX (Euronext: NANO - NASDAQ: NBTX - the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biotechnology company pioneering physics-based approaches to expand treatment possibilities for patients with cancer and other major diseases, today announced updated results from patients with anti-PD-1-resistant advanced primary cutaneous melanoma treated in the ongoing Phase 1 Study 1100. The study evaluates JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3), which works in the presence of radiotherapy, followed by an immune checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) in patients with advanced solid tumors. The data were presented by Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center, in a poster session on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (“ESMO”) in Madrid, Spain.

ABSTRACT #3956: Safety and Anti-Tumor Activity of NBTXR3/SBRT with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Anti-PD-1 Resistant Melanoma: Results from a Phase I Dose Expansion

J. Chan, J. Lee, A. Lam, A. Daud, F. Collichio, H. Yu, P. Mody, J. Weiss, S. Moschos, S. Powell, S. Peck, M. Lohr, E. Redstone, Z. Li, W. Smith, A. Juloori, R. Gineste, D. Rolando, A. Rosenberg and C. Shen. UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center; UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Sanford Cancer Center; St Luke's University Hospital; The University of Chicago; Nanobiotix

Patients with advanced anti-PD-1 resistant primary cutaneous melanoma whose disease has progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy have a poor prognosis; published series report a median progression-free survival of approximately three months1 and a median overall survival of approximately one year2 in this setting. Melanoma has historically been considered radioresistant, and higher radiation doses are often limited by exposure of the surrounding healthy tissue.

“Patients whose melanoma has progressed on anti-PD-1 therapy, and often on several other immunotherapies as well, have limited options left,” said Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center “In this study, a single injection followed by a short course of stereotactic radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of tumor sizes and locations, and we saw responses in lesions that were injected and in lesions that were not. The observed increase in IL-1β suggests treatment-related immune activation that warrants further investigation. These are early data from a single-arm study, and they support testing the approach in a randomized trial.”

All 24 heavily pre-treated patients had advanced primary cutaneous melanoma resistant to anti-PD-1; 14 had stage IV disease. Most had received other immunotherapies before enrolling, including anti-CTLA-4 (50%), anti-LAG-3 (33.3%) and T-VEC (25%), and 87.5% had received immunotherapy as their most recent therapy. Patients received a one-time intratumoral injection of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) at the recommended Phase 2 dose (33% of gross tumor volume), followed by stereotactic body radiotherapy (“SBRT”) to the injected lesion and then nivolumab or pembrolizumab. Investigators observed an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy.

Safety and Feasibility

Treatment consisting of a single intratumoral JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) injection, followed by a short course of radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of melanoma lesions, providing a minimally invasive treatment approach with an acceptable safety profile. No new safety signals have been observed.

Preliminary Efficacy

An Overall Response Rate (ORR) of 41.7% (10/24 patients) was observed. Responses were observed in both injected (ORR 45.8%; 11/24 evaluable patients) and non-injected lesions (ORR 30.0%; 3/10 evaluable patients).

Median Progression Free Survival (PFS) was 6.9 months, while median Overall Survival reached 17.8 months.

Exploratory Immune Profiling

In an exploratory analysis of plasma samples from a subset of patients (n=8), IL-1β showed the largest increase from baseline among the cytokines evaluated. Published research has linked IL-1β to treatment-induced anti-tumor immunity through its role in connecting innate immune activation to the priming of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells.3

"This updated analysis, with more patients and longer follow-up, builds on the first data we reported with consistent safety and an improvement in Overall Survival relative to the first data reported," said Louis Kayitalire, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Nanobiotix. "Responses were again seen in patients whose disease had progressed after multiple prior therapies, including in lesions that were not injected. Together with the exploratory cytokine data, these findings warrant further evaluation of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) followed by anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma."

Overall, the acceptable safety profile and early efficacy observed by investigators in these preliminary findings provide promising signals of activity and warrant further evaluation in larger randomized trials.

About JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3)

JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) is a novel, potentially first-in-class oncology product composed of functionalized hafnium oxide nanoparticles administered via one-time intratumoral injection and designed to work in the presenced of radiotherapy. The product candidate’s mechanism of action (MoA) is designed to induce significant tumor cell death in the injected tumor when in the presence of radiotherapy, subsequently triggering adaptive immune response and long-term anti-cancer memory. Proof-of-concept was demonstrated in a randomized Phase 2/3 soft tissue sarcoma study sponsored by Nanobiotix in 2018.

JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) is being evaluated across multiple solid tumor indications as a single agent or combination therapy. Given the Company’s focus areas, and balanced against the scalable potential of NBTXR3, Nanobiotix has engaged in a collaboration strategy to expand development of the product candidate in parallel with its priority development pathways. Pursuant to this strategy, in 2019 Nanobiotix entered into a broad, comprehensive clinical research collaboration with The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center to sponsor several Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies evaluating JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) across tumor types and therapeutic combinations.

In February 2020, the United States Food and Drug Administration granted regulatory Fast Track designation for the investigation of NBTXR3 with or without cetuximab, for the treatment of patients with locally advanced HNSCC who are not eligible for platinum-based chemotherapy.

In 2023, Nanobiotix announced a license agreement for the global development and commercialization of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) with Janssen Pharmaceutica NV, a Johnson & Johnson company. Studies being led by Johnson & Johnson include NANORAY-312 (NCT04892173), a global, randomized Phase 3 study in platinum-based chemotherapy-ineligible, locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancers; LUMIRAY (NCT07219212), a global, phase 1b, open-label study in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell cancers; and CONVERGE (NCT06667908), a phase 2, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study in locally advanced and unresectable Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

About NANOBIOTIX

Nanobiotix is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company pioneering disruptive, physics-based therapeutic approaches to revolutionize treatment outcomes for millions of patients; supported by people committed to making a difference for humanity. The Company’s philosophy is rooted in the concept of pushing past the boundaries of what is known to expand possibilities for human life.

Incorporated in 2003, Nanobiotix is headquartered in Paris, France and is listed on Euronext Paris since 2012 and on the Nasdaq Global Select Market in New York City since December 2020. The Company has subsidiaries in Cambridge, Massachusetts (United States) amongst other locations.

Nanobiotix is the owner of more than 30 umbrella patents associated with three (3) nanotechnology platforms with applications in 1) oncology; 2) bioavailability and biodistribution; and 3) disorders of the central nervous system.

data.title: Genmab and Incyte Announce Clinical Trial Collaboration in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
data.description:
Media Release

COPENHAGEN, Denmark and WILMINGTON, Del.; October 24, 2026

  • Phase 1/2 study will evaluate petosemtamab plus INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in first-line KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC)

Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and Incyte (Nasdaq: INCY) today announced a clinical trial collaboration to evaluate petosemtamab, Genmab’s investigational IgG1-bispecific antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5), in combination with INCB161734, Incyte’s investigational, potent and selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, and standard-of-care chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring a KRAS G12D mutation, an area with substantial unmet medical need.

“This collaboration supports our broader development strategy for petosemtamab as we explore its potential across treatment settings and in novel combinations,” said Judith Klimovsky, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Development Officer, Genmab. “Partnering with Incyte enables us to evaluate this investigational combination in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer, reflecting our commitment to research collaborations aimed at expanding potential treatment options for more patients.”

“Metastatic colorectal cancer remains difficult-to-treat, underscoring the importance of evaluating novel combinations grounded in complementary scientific approaches with the potential to enhance efficacy,” said Pablo J. Cagnoni, M.D., President, Incyte and Global Head of Research and Development. “Our collaboration with Genmab will explore the potential of combining KRAS G12D inhibition with LGR5-targeted EGFR inhibition and standard-of-care chemotherapy, with the goal of advancing a new first-line treatment approach for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer.”

Under the collaboration, Genmab will conduct the Phase 1/2 study evaluating petosemtamab in combination with INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated mCRC in the first-line setting. Incyte will co-fund the study and provide clinical supply of INCB161734.

KRAS mutations occur in approximately 40% of colorectal cancers, with G12D being the most common KRAS mutation. These cancers are associated with poor prognosis, underscoring the need for new treatment approaches. The collaboration reflects a shared focus on investigating whether agents with distinct and potentially complementary mechanisms, combined with standard-of-care chemotherapy, may offer a path toward a new treatment option for patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer.

About Petosemtamab (GEN1158)

Petosemtamab is an investigational human IgG1-based bispecific antibody targeting the EGFR and the LGR5 and designed to support multiple anti-tumor mechanisms. It inhibits EGFR-mediated signaling by engaging a unique site on the receptor to prevent ligand binding. In addition, petosemtamab triggers EGFR degradation in cancer stem-like cells expressing both EGFR and LGR5. Petosemtamab is also engineered to enhance innate immune-mediated activity through interactions with macrophages and natural killer cells. It is currently being investigated in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and other solid tumors, including colorectal cancer (CRC). Petosemtamab is being evaluated in combination with chemotherapy in two Phase 3 trials in first- and second-line RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic CRC. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

About INCB161734

INCB161734 is an investigational, novel, selective and orally bioavailable small molecule ON/OFF KRAS G12D inhibitor. KRAS is one of the most frequently altered oncogenic drivers across solid tumors, and the KRAS G12D mutation is among the most common KRAS alterations, occurring in approximately 40% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and approximately 15% of colorectal cancer (CRC) cases.

INCB161734 is being evaluated in the global Phase 3 DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) study which is currently enrolling patients with previously untreated KRAS G12D-mutated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of INCB161734 in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy.

INCB161734 is also being evaluated as a monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy (gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel [GEMNabP] or modified FOLFIRINOX [mFOLFIRINOX]), in an ongoing open-label Phase 1 study across KRAS G12D-mutated solid tumors (NCT06179160).

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com or follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Incyte is redefining what’s possible in biopharmaceutical innovation. Through deep scientific expertise and a relentless focus on patients, we have built an established portfolio of first-in-class medicines and an extensive portfolio of next-generation medicines across our key franchises: Hematology, Oncology and Inflammation & Autoimmunity.

data.title: VRL Logistics to buy back 87.5 lakh shares at ₹320 per share
data.description:
VRL Logistics’ share buyback offer will open on October 27 and close on November 2, with the company proposing to repurchase up to 87.5 lakh equity shares at ₹320 apiece, according to its letter of offer filed on Saturday, October 24.

The buyback represents 5% of the company’s paid-up equity share capital as of March 31, 2026. The company will spend up to ₹280 crore on the offer, excluding transaction costs. The record date to determine eligible shareholders was October 22.

VRL Logistics said the buyback is aimed at returning surplus cash to shareholders and improving returns. “The current Buyback proposal is in line with the Company’s capital allocation practices of returning excess cash to shareholders, thereby increasing shareholder value in the longer term, and improving the Return on Equity,” it said in the letter of offer.

The promoter and promoter group have decided not to participate in the buyback.

Small shareholders have an indicative entitlement of 14 shares for every 99 shares held on the record date, while other eligible shareholders have an indicative entitlement of 19 shares for every 154 shares held. Shareholders holding up to 750 shares on the record date have been classified as small shareholders.

The offer will be carried out through the tender offer route on a proportionate basis, subject to the reservation for small shareholders. The last date for settlement of bids and payment to eligible shareholders is November 9.

VRL Logistics said the buyback will be funded from free reserves or other permitted sources, and that borrowed funds from banks and financial institutions will not be used.
